newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends at seven-month high.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends at seven-month high.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed at a seven-month high on Tuesday on exporter activities and dealers said the local unit might test new highs in the near term.

The local rate closed at T$27.443, off an intra-day high of T$27.428, compared with Monday's T$27.471. Tuesday's close was the highest level since a peak of T$27.418 on May 24, 1996. Turnover through dealers was an active US$533 million.
"The central appeared to offer U.S. dollars before the close to slow down the Taiwan dollar appreciation," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
However, some dealers said the strong U.S. dollar against the Japanese yen in overseas markets should limit the local unit's gains.
"The market has been quiet for a long time and some players grabbed the chance to engage in the foreign exchange market today," said another dealer.
"But they will also cautiously watch the central bank's movements at the same time," he said, noting the central bank's long-term policy of keeping a stable foreign exchange rate.
Initial resistance was seen at T$27.40.
